system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Biglari Holdings Inc. (successor public entity) realized record, fiscal year 2021 (~3.5 years after closing)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The pre-transaction legal entity terminated its
> own SEC registration shortly after the transaction, but the successor public parent
> created by the transaction continued to file periodic reports under a new SEC filer
> identity; the realized record below is drawn from that successor's fiscal-year 2021
> Form 10-K (filed 2022-02-28), the filing falling within a fixed ~3-5-year window after
> the closing-era transaction. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the
> transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- The pre-transaction legal entity (Commission File Number 0-8445) filed a Form 15-12G on 2018-08-08, terminating registration of its securities under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act. [SRC: SEC accession 0001341004-18-000494, Form 15-12G]
- A successor public holding company, also named "Biglari Holdings Inc." (Commission File Number 001-38477, a distinct EIN of 82-3784946), continued to file periodic reports with the SEC in the years following the transaction, so a public financial and operating record for the surviving businesses is observable. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]
- As reported on the cover of that Form 10-K, the successor company's Class A and Class B common stock traded on the NYSE under the symbols "BH.A" and "BH" respectively. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]
- Sardar Biglari was identified as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the successor company as of the fiscal-year 2021 report. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]

## Realized financial record (fiscal year 2021)
- For fiscal year 2021, the successor company reported total revenues of $366,106 thousand and net earnings attributable to shareholders of $35,478 thousand ($111.83 per equivalent Class A share), compared with a net loss of $37,989 thousand the prior fiscal year and net earnings of $45,380 thousand the fiscal year before that. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021, Item 6 Selected Financial Data]
- Net earnings attributable to shareholders for fiscal year 2021 were disaggregated as: restaurant operations $11,235 thousand, insurance $11,290 thousand, oil and gas $7,528 thousand, brand licensing $2,364 thousand, interest expense $(841) thousand, and corporate and other $(9,829) thousand (total operating businesses $21,747 thousand), plus investment partnership gains of $8,899 thousand and investment gains of $4,832 thousand. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]
- At fiscal year-end 2021, total assets were $894,807 thousand and total shareholders' equity was $587,696 thousand. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021, Item 6 Selected Financial Data]
- The company employed 2,633 persons as of December 31, 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]

## Realized operating record — restaurant segment
- As of December 31, 2021, the restaurant subsidiaries operated a combined 577 units; the larger chain had 199 company-operated restaurants (of which 42 were closed, with the company stating an intent to refranchise a majority of them), 159 franchise-partner units, and 178 traditional franchise units. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]
- The Form 10-K attributes elevated asset impairments in fiscal year 2020 primarily to "dining room closures and uncertainties caused by the pandemic," with asset impairments decreasing by $19,011 thousand in fiscal year 2021 compared with fiscal year 2020. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]

## Items not documented in the reviewed record
- No divestiture, dissolution, or wind-down of any business held at the earlier reorganization (restaurant, insurance, oil and gas, media/licensing) is described in the fiscal-year 2021 Form 10-K; the insurance segment as reported still comprised both of its constituent underwriting entities. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]
- No transitional-services or shared-substrate agreement from the earlier restructuring is referenced as still in effect or as having caused any disclosed disruption in this filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The publicly observable record for the surviving businesses over the reviewed post-transaction period shows continuity of the pre-transaction operating businesses and leadership under a successor public parent, a swing from a net loss in fiscal year 2020 to net earnings of $35,478 thousand in fiscal year 2021, and a documented partial contraction in company-operated restaurant count (42 of 199 units closed as of fiscal year-end 2021) alongside an ongoing franchise-partner conversion program, with no divestiture or dissolution of the businesses documented in the reviewed filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001726173-22-000004, Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021]

[SLICE END]
